"BRAIN DEATH" WAS INVENTED IN 1968 by 13 men at Harvard Medical School — not because science proved these patients were dead, but to free up ICU beds and harvest their organs.

Their original draft stated bluntly: 
“There is great need for the tissues and organs of the hopelessly comatose in order to restore health to those who are still salvageable.”

That sentence was edited out before publication because it was “too telling.”

The final JAMA paper never called these patients dead. It described them as “desperately injured” and “a burden to themselves and others.”

These people have beating hearts, warm bodies, and circulating blood. Some “brain dead” mothers have even carried babies to term on ventilators.

They are NOT dead. They are severely brain-injured — and this redefinition stripped them of legal protections so their organs could be taken while they were still alive.

This wasn’t pure medicine. It was utilitarian engineering to serve the transplant industry.

Your loved one could be next. You could be next.

💎 How GRAM became GRAM

TON blockchain and its native token Gram have a fascinating history. Here's how crypto in Telegram evolved.

📖 First came the name
In 2017, Pavel Durov was choosing a name for Telegram's new cryptocurrency.

The idea was to give it a simple, familiar name that would fit naturally into everyday life. That's how Gram was born.

👥 Then came the community
In 2019, Telegram stepped away from the project, and the community continued developing the open-source technology independently. The blockchain later became The Open Network, with Toncoin as its native token.

Toncoin wasn't immediately listed on major exchanges, so @wallet was created as a simple way to buy the coin right inside the messenger.

🔄 The long-awaited return
In spring 2026, Durov announced the MTONGA plan, Make TON Great Again, with 7 steps.

Telegram returned to the project: became the network's largest validator, replaced TON Foundation and taking a leading role in TON's development. The community voted to restore the original name: Toncoin became GRAM again.

⭐️ Gram wallet
Continuing the MTONGA plan, Durov announced a built-in non-custodial wallet. It's already available to select groups and will reach millions of users over the coming weeks.

A new chapter is unfolding in the ecosystem, and together with Telegram's Gram wallet, we'll be shaping the crypto experience for users 👥

The European Central Bank has launched Pontes, a platform connecting DLT market infrastructure directly to its payment rails for wholesale tokenized asset settlement in central-bank money — no stablecoins required. The ECB is also preparing to invest part of its €23 billion own-funds portfolio in digital securities.

Pontes will expand services and operating hours gradually, with full implementation targeted for 2028. It's entirely separate from the retail digital euro pilot, still slated for 2027. Central banks moving to make blockchain settlement boring and institutional — which is probably exactly the point.

Bitcoin’s broader daily structure remains constructive despite the decline. BTC is trading slightly above its 10-day simple moving average at $78,732, while the 20-day SMA is much lower at $70,242.

🌐 Coldcard hacker uses THORChain to swap stolen BTC 

📣 A hacker associated with the third wave of Coldcard wallet thefts began converting stolen Bitcoin into Ether through THORChain on Sept. 3, according to Galaxy Research’s Alex Thorn. The transactions moved approximately 10% of the Bitcoin controlled by that attacker. Roughly 90% remained at its original addresses when he published the update. 

🔖 Researchers traced the swaps through THORChain to a newly identified Ethereum address. Thorn said he shared the address with law enforcement, crypto companies and other organizations monitoring the stolen assets. However, not every transaction succeeded. Thorn said the hacker appeared to be experiencing technical problems while attempting to process the swaps.

🔔 The cause of the refunds was not immediately confirmed. Possible explanations include liquidity limitations, transaction settings or protocol safeguards, but no verified technical assessment had established the reason. The movement represented the first detected onchain transfer from the original addresses associated with the first three attack waves, according to Thorn. Analysts will now monitor whether the resulting ETH moves to centralized exchanges, bridges or privacy services.
